title: Buying in the EU: your rights under EU law
lead: These rules apply to all products of this type sold in the EU. They are not a rating of this model and not a prediction of how long it will last.
guarantee: Legal guarantee: if the product is faulty or not as described, the seller must repair or replace it — or, if that is not possible, lower the price or refund you. This applies for a minimum period set by EU law, whatever the manufacturer's own warranty says.
spare: Spare parts: the manufacturer must keep certain spare parts available to repairers for a period set by EU ecodesign rules, also after the model is no longer sold.
repairInfo: Repair information: the manufacturer must give professional repairers access to repair and maintenance information.
updates: Software: the manufacturer must keep providing operating-system updates for a period set by EU rules after the model is no longer sold.
repair: Repair after the guarantee: under the EU right-to-repair rules, the manufacturer must offer to repair this type of product at a reasonable price, also after the legal guarantee has ended.
note: A short summary for information only, not legal advice. The exact periods, conditions and exceptions are in the official texts linked here and in the law of your country. Ask the seller or the manufacturer about the guarantee for your purchase.
